test(ErdosProblems/676): prove residue criterion and finite exceptions (#7428)

Proves that the representation in Erdős Problem 676 is equivalent to the
existence of a prime `p` with `p^2 ≤ n` and `n % p^2 < p`. The lower
bound retains the source's requirement `a ≥ 1`. Adds kernel-checked
tests showing that 35 and 899 have no such representation.

This is a partial contribution. The eventual representation question
remains open, and its statement and placeholder proof are unchanged.

Validation: the exact three new theorem bodies compile with Lean 4.33.1
and `-DwarningAsError=true` using the pinned Mathlib. All three axiom
reports contain only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
The finite checks use `decide`, not `native_decide`.

GitHub CI passed the project build and script tests for commit
833da2e20d8f6306ddc57d8c9f641f6f82c4638e. The local repository build
exhausted memory in unchanged dependencies; the standalone proof checks
above completed successfully. The PR remains a draft because this is a
partial contribution to the requested full solution.

AI-assisted contribution using Codex. The source correspondence and
finite statements received a separate automated mathematical audit.

files.patch:
@@ -37,6 +37,47 @@ namespace Erdos676
 
 open Filter
 
+/-- An integer has a representation $ap^2+b$ with $p$ prime, $a \geq 1$, and $b < p$
+if and only if $p^2 \leq n$ and $n \bmod p^2 < p$ for some prime $p$. -/
+@[category test, AMS 11]
+theorem representation_iff_mod (n : ℕ) :
+    (∃ a p b : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ b < p ∧ n = a * p ^ 2 + b) ↔
+      ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ^ 2 ≤ n ∧ n % p ^ 2 < p := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨a, p, b, hp, ha, hb, rfl⟩
+    refine ⟨p, hp, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · nlinarith
+    · have hb' : b < p ^ 2 := by
+        have := hp.two_le
+        nlinarith
+      simpa [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hb'] using hb
+  · rintro ⟨p, hp, hn, hr⟩
+    refine ⟨n / p ^ 2, p, n % p ^ 2, hp, ?_, hr, ?_⟩
+    · exact Nat.div_pos hn (pow_pos hp.pos _)
+    · simpa [Nat.mul_comm, Nat.add_comm] using (Nat.mod_add_div n (p ^ 2)).symm
+
+/-- The integer $35$ has no representation $ap^2+b$ of the required form. -/
+@[category test, AMS 11]
+theorem not_representable_35 :
+    ¬ ∃ a p b : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ b < p ∧ 35 = a * p ^ 2 + b := by
+  rw [representation_iff_mod]
+  rintro ⟨p, hp, hn, hr⟩
+  have hp6 : p < 6 := by nlinarith
+  have hc : ∀ q : Fin 6, ¬ (q.val.Prime ∧ q.val ^ 2 ≤ 35 ∧ 35 % q.val ^ 2 < q.val) :=
+    by decide
+  exact hc ⟨p, hp6⟩ ⟨hp, hn, hr⟩
+
+/-- The integer $899$ has no representation $ap^2+b$ of the required form. -/
+@[category test, AMS 11]
+theorem not_representable_899 :
+    ¬ ∃ a p b : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ a ∧ b < p ∧ 899 = a * p ^ 2 + b := by
+  rw [representation_iff_mod]
+  rintro ⟨p, hp, hn, hr⟩
+  have hp30 : p < 30 := by nlinarith
+  have hc : ∀ q : Fin 30, ¬ (q.val.Prime ∧ q.val ^ 2 ≤ 899 ∧ 899 % q.val ^ 2 < q.val) :=
+    by decide
+  exact hc ⟨p, hp30⟩ ⟨hp, hn, hr⟩
+
 /-- Is every sufficiently large integer of the form $ap^2+b$ for some prime $p$ and integers
 $a \geq 1$ and $0 \leq b < p$? -/
 @[category research open, question, AMS 11]
